description:
What happens when extraordinary talent isn't recognized?

Before becoming one of the world's most celebrated young mathematicians, Wang Hong struggled through college, questioned her future, and nearly gave up mathematics altogether. At China's most prestigious university, she often felt invisible. Years later, under a different academic environment and a mentor who encouraged exploration instead of constant competition, she made a breakthrough that earned mathematics' highest honor.

Her story is often discussed alongside that of Deng Yu, another outstanding mathematician who chose to leave Peking University and continue his education at MIT before building a distinguished research career.

In this documentary, we compare two remarkable journeys to explore a broader question: How should great mathematicians be developed? Through competition and selection—or through mentorship, patience, and intellectual freedom?
